name: W H Rogers Sheet Metal Inc
old_description: technologies to accommodate your needs. Working from your design
about:
Founded in 1966 in Charlotte, North Carolina, W H Rogers Sheet Metal Inc has operated as a custom metal fabrication and machine shop for over five decades. The company is located in Charlotte and serves customers throughout the Carolinas.

The shop provides custom fabrication from customer drawings or with design assistance from its in-house CAD department. Its capabilities include fiber laser cutting (6,000 watt and 4,000 watt systems), shearing with plate shears and angle rolls, press brake forming, punching, cold sawing, CNC vertical machining, CNC turning with automated bar feed, manual milling and turning, and MIG, TIG, and stick welding. The facility houses a range of equipment for both large and small metalworking jobs.

W H Rogers Sheet Metal serves industrial clients across the Carolinas, producing custom metal parts and assemblies for a variety of applications. The company's ASME certification under Boiler & Pressure Vessel Code Section IX and B31.3 qualifies it for pressure vessel and piping work.

The business emphasizes its role as a proven and dependable fabrication source, offering a full range of metalworking services under one roof. President Wendell Canipe leads a team that includes estimator Jason Martin, CNC programmer Joe Mitchell, and production manager Mark Zimmerman.

name: W&W | AFCO Steel
old_description: Setting the standard in steel design, fabrication, and erection since 1909.
about:
W&W | AFCO Steel operates from Van Buren, Arkansas, where it was founded in 1909. Over more than a century, the company has grown into a full-service structural steel contractor capable of handling design, fabrication, and erection under one roof.

The firm’s core services cover structural steel design, shop fabrication, and field erection for large-scale projects. Notable work includes the 24,000-ton steel package for the MSG Sphere in Las Vegas, the Las Vegas Convention Center expansion, the Kaufmann Performing Arts Museum, the I-235 train bridge in Iowa, and the renovation of Chicago’s Soldier Field.

Clients come from sectors such as entertainment venues, convention centers, cultural institutions, transportation infrastructure, and sports facilities. The company typically partners with general contractors, developers, and public agencies that require complex steel structures delivered on challenging sites.

W&W | AFCO Steel differentiates itself through a relationship-driven, American-made philosophy, focusing on the most complex structures and the most difficult site conditions.

about:
Based in Hurricane, West Virginia, W.V. Riddle Electrical LLC operates as a local electrical contractor serving the surrounding region. The company's founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed, but it presents itself as a certified, bonded, and licensed provider of electrical services.

The firm delivers a broad range of electrical work, including wiring upgrades and repairs, electrical panel upgrades, circuit breaker installation, lighting fixture and switch installation, exterior and landscape lighting, ceiling fan and appliance installation, standby generator and emergency generator installation, structured cabling, home automation, surge protection, electrical inspections, code violation remediation, and 24/7 emergency repair. Services extend to both new construction and remodeling projects, as well as hot tub, spa, and in-floor heating electrical work.

W.V. Riddle Electrical serves residential homeowners and commercial clients, from single-family houses to larger businesses requiring complex electrical overhauls. The company notes that it handles jobs of any size, citing examples such as kitchen renovations, commercial lighting retrofits, and emergency power restoration for both property types.

The contractor emphasizes free upfront estimates, rigorous safety gear protocols, extensively trained employees, and a policy of immediate communication if unforeseen issues arise. It states that its technicians are certified, bonded, and licensed, and that honesty and integrity guide every project.

name: WCC Brands Custom Apparel
old_description: (Drive under 151, take the first left and we are the 4th building in the industrial park)
about:
WCC Brands Custom Apparel operates from Kieler, Wisconsin, where it has provided screen printing and embroidery services for over 30 years. The company serves schools, universities, local businesses, and international corporations from its facility in the industrial park off County Highway H.

The shop runs commercial-grade, fully automatic screen printing presses and embroidery machines, supported by an in-house design and production team. Its capabilities include screen printing, embroidery, heat transfer, and promotional product sourcing, allowing it to handle custom apparel and accessory decoration from concept through finished goods.

Customers range from educational institutions ordering spirit wear to corporate clients needing branded uniforms and industrial buyers requiring ANSI-rated high-visibility garments for job-site safety. The company also supplies promotional items such as bags, packs, and duffels.

WCC Brands emphasizes a team-based approach, with responsive in-house staff and automated equipment aimed at consistent, reliable production. The business was built to extend client brands through apparel and promotional items, combining design support with decoration expertise.

name: WMK & Co
old_description: Trusted Montana steel fabrication and structural erection services since 1992 across the region
about:
WMK & Co. was founded in 1992 and is headquartered in Billings, Montana. The company operates additional facilities in Great Falls, Kalispell, and Butte, allowing it to serve projects across Montana and into Idaho and Washington. Ownership details are not publicly disclosed, and the founders are not named in available sources.

The firm specializes in structural steel fabrication, custom metalwork, steel erection, and design services. Its in-house detailing department and a team of more than 50 professionals manage projects from concept through completion. The acquisition of Stevens Steel West expanded both capacity and geographic reach in the Northwest.

WMK & Co. serves contractors, engineers, and project managers in commercial construction, architectural, environmental, military, and industrial sectors. Projects range from commercial buildings to specialized infrastructure across Montana, Idaho, and Washington.

The company states its mission is to deliver precision steel fabrication and erection at competitive cost while maintaining the highest standards of quality, safety, and customer satisfaction. Safety is described as core to its operations, and it emphasizes certified processes (AISC and AWS) to meet industry standards.

name: WTC Fiber
old_description: World-class connectivity with premier customer service, expert installation, and no risk or obligations.
about:
WTC Fiber, headquartered in Wamego, Kansas, was founded in 1912 as a local telephone company. Over more than a century it has expanded from a single exchange into a regional telecommunications provider.

Today the company builds and operates fiber-to-the-home networks, delivers residential and business broadband, digital cable TV, and voice services, and manages large-scale public Wi-Fi deployments. In 2025 it deployed 1.7 million feet of fiber and served more than 15,000 customers across Pottawatomie, Riley, Geary, Wabaunsee, and Shawnee counties, with 400-plus managed systems ranging from school districts to healthcare clinics.

Its customer base spans residential subscribers, small and mid-sized businesses, educational institutions, medical facilities, and municipal agencies. Notable projects include a $830,000 community-wide public Wi-Fi network covering 124 locations in Manhattan and Riley County, and a partnership providing connectivity at Kansas State University's Tointon Family Stadium.

WTC Fiber emphasizes local, contract-free service backed by a 24/7 help desk and a published Customer Care Commitment. Its mission stresses shareholder value, employee support, and corporate citizenship, with a stated goal of delivering affordable, high-quality telecommunications using the latest technology around the clock.

name: WWW Electronics Inc.
old_description: Family Owned contract manufacturing firm serving your printed circuit design, assembly, and testing needs since 1969.
about:
WWW Electronics Inc. was founded in 1969 in Charlottesville, Virginia, as a family-owned contract manufacturing firm. The company has operated continuously from its facility on Dobleann Drive, providing printed circuit design, assembly, and testing services for over five decades.

The company's core production capabilities span surface-mount and through-hole PCB assembly, cable and harness assembly, chassis wiring, mechanical assembly, and final product integration. It also offers enclosure customization including machining and silk-screening, conformal coating, and potting. Beyond fabrication, WWW Electronics provides engineering support such as multi-layer PCB layout, circuit design, schematic capture, embedded firmware development, and design-for-manufacturability and testability analysis. A reverse-engineering service can recreate schematics, bills of materials, and Gerber files from existing board samples. The firm emphasizes flexibility, handling runs from a few prototypes to thousands of completed assemblies.

While the company does not publicly list specific industry verticals, its cage code (75T85) and UEI registration indicate it serves government and defense-related customers alongside commercial clients. Typical engagements include full turnkey PCB assembly, custom cable builds, and complete box-build projects for original equipment manufacturers and other electronics integrators.

For higher-volume programs, the team develops custom test fixtures and automated test software to improve throughput and data logging. The engineering group works directly with customers on design optimization, and the reverse-engineering capability addresses legacy product sustainment needs.

name: Wagner Food Equipment
old_description: Founded by Richard Walton Wagner, our company was built on the promise of "Quality Without Exception." For five decades, we have remained a trusted, independent partner for Virginia’s foodservice industry.
about:
Wagner Food Equipment was founded by Richard Walton Wagner in Roanoke, Virginia, over five decades ago with a commitment to "Quality Without Exception." The company remains an independent, locally owned service provider for the region's foodservice industry.

The company specializes in repair and maintenance of commercial kitchen equipment, including cooking, refrigeration, dishwashing, food preparation, bakery, and weigh-and-wrap systems. As an authorized Hobart sales and service representative, Wagner supplies OEM parts and provides factory-trained technician support. The team comprises 25 factory-trained technicians with over 200 combined years of experience, operating from four regional offices across Southwest Virginia.

Wagner serves commercial kitchens throughout Southwest Virginia, covering 27 counties and 16 independent cities such as Roanoke, Lynchburg, Danville, and Harrisonburg. Customers include restaurants, supermarkets, and institutional foodservice operations.

The company emphasizes a "Quality Without Exception" philosophy, focusing on reducing downtime through expert repairs and genuine OEM parts. Technicians are noted for deep mechanical knowledge of electrical, gas, and steam systems, and an understanding of high-volume kitchen workflows.

old_description: Wako Electronics designs and manufactures bimetal thermostats,
about:
Wako Electronics USA Inc. operates from Louisville, Kentucky, in eastern Jefferson County. The company was founded in 1988 as the U.S. subsidiary of Japan's Wako Seiki Co., Ltd., a producer of automated assembly equipment. Ownership remains with the Japanese parent, and no founder names are disclosed in public records.

The company designs and manufactures bimetal thermostats, employing statistical process control (SPC) across its manufacturing operations. Its capabilities include test and inspection (incoming and outgoing), a supplier certification program, and 100% product traceability. The Louisville facility houses full production and assembly; the global organization reports approximately 80,000 employees.

Wako serves the automotive industry, with a client base that includes Delphi Automotive Systems and Michigan Automotive. The company partners with suppliers worldwide to source materials and components that meet its quality and cost targets.

Wako emphasizes total cost productivity, material quality, and reliability as the foundation of its manufacturing philosophy, aiming to transform into an innovative industry leader that places customer satisfaction at the center.

name: Walco Electric Co.
old_description: Walco is a diversified high-technology company that specializes in the optimization of rotating electro-mechanical apparatus and automated process equipment. With 87 years of
about:
Walco Electric Co. opened in 1931 in Providence, Rhode Island, when founder Edmund Waldman began manufacturing radio antenna kits before pivoting to electric motor repair for the region’s wire and textile mills. The shop grew alongside the port of Providence into one of the Northeast’s largest electrical apparatus service facilities, adding a maintenance machine shop, electrical contracting, and an electronic motor control group over the next four decades.

Today Walco operates through three groups: Automation and Controls, which provides systems engineering, drive integration, and motion control as a Siemens Solution Partner with more than 1,500 drives installed worldwide; Industrial Power Systems, delivering electrical and mechanical maintenance, repair, and on‑site service; and Rail Transportation, which rebuilds, rewinds, and remanufactures AC and DC traction motors, generators, and auxiliary equipment at what the company calls New England’s largest transit motor rebuilding facility, staffed by over 40 technicians working three shifts with 24/7 emergency coverage.

The rail group serves mass‑transit agencies and Class I railroads, including the MBTA, SEPTA, Metro‑North, New York City Transit, and the Cleveland, Pittsburgh, and Baltimore authorities. Automation and Controls customers span metals, paper, plastics, converting, textiles, and roofing industries, while Industrial Power Systems supports national and international industrial plants.

Walco traces its differentiation to a founding emphasis on integrity and customer service, encapsulated in the slogan “Never Underestimate the Power of Total Commitment,” and highlights its AAR M‑1003 certification, ISO‑compliant quality program, and status as the only Siemens motion partner in the Northeast.
